differences.title: 1. DATA MODEL
differences.leftDesc: Yjs uses a shared document tree with nested types (Text, Map, Array). Operations are applied directly to this tree structure for efficient updates.
differences.rightDesc: Automerge uses a history of operations (a log) that are applied to an immutable document state. It builds the current state by replaying operations.

differences.title: 2. CONFLICT RESOLUTION
differences.leftDesc: Yjs relies on timestamping and last-write-wins for simple conflicts, especially with text edits. Concurrent edits might lose one specific change.
differences.rightDesc: Automerge uses a sophisticated CRDT algorithm that guarantees convergence for any concurrent operation, ensuring all changes are eventually merged correctly.

differences.title: 3. PERFORMANCE
differences.leftDesc: Yjs is highly optimized for fast local updates and minimal overhead, especially for large documents and frequent edits, due to its tree structure.
differences.rightDesc: Automerge excels at merging changes from multiple clients efficiently. The log-based approach can have higher initial state loading or replay costs.

differences.title: 4. DATA TYPES
differences.leftDesc: Yjs provides rich, mutable data types like Text, Map, Array, and XML. These are optimized for specific collaborative editing patterns.
differences.rightDesc: Automerge primarily deals with JSON-like primitives and nested objects/arrays. Custom types require manual implementation on top of these basics.

differences.title: 5. STATE MANAGEMENT
differences.leftDesc: Yjs maintains an in-memory representation of the document, which is directly mutated by operations. This offers a simpler mental model for local state.
differences.rightDesc: Automerge works with immutable document states. Each operation produces a new state, facilitating easier debugging and time-travel capabilities.

differences.title: 6. SYNCHRONIZATION
differences.leftDesc: Yjs is designed for direct peer-to-peer synchronization. It efficiently serializes and deserializes updates between connected clients.
differences.rightDesc: Automerge serializes operations into messages that can be sent over any transport. Its focus is on the CRDT logic itself.

differences.title: 7. COMMUNITY & ECOSYSTEM
differences.leftDesc: Yjs has a large, active community and a mature ecosystem with integrations for various frameworks and storage solutions.
differences.rightDesc: Automerge has a strong core and is gaining traction, particularly in projects valuing immutable state and robust conflict resolution.
